items.original_text: Estimated time: 240 to 570 days. Estimated government cost: $8,300 to $24,000. Notes: The critical path is the Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days per the catalog) and the ABC Type 42 license transfer (60–150 days), which must be done sequentially or in parallel depending on Planning's confirmation that the CUA can be filed before the license is escrowed. The Place of Entertainment permit (45–120 days) will run in parallel with the CUA or immediately after. Building permit plan review (14–120 days) and DPH plan check (21–60 days) typically overlap with the CUA hearing process. ABC's timeline may extend by 1–3 months (30–90 additional days) if a Public Convenience or Necessity finding is required due to the nine on-sale licenses within 500 ft. The minimum timeline assumes no PCN delay, over-the-counter DPH and building approvals, and a straightforward CUA hearing with no continuances (about 8 months total). The maximum timeline assumes a PCN referral, full plan review with revisions, a continued CUA hearing, and ABC transfer delays (about 19 months). outcomes.original: Filing step: File a Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning for a Bar use at 995 Valencia St, including the change of use from Restaurant, with plans showing the bar layout, seating, kitchen, and performance area. What to say: State that the concept is a 40-seat beer-and-wine bar with a limited kitchen serving small plates, live entertainment with amplified sound, and a 1 a.m. closing time. Commit to using a Type 42 license transferred from another bar within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD per Planning Code § 249.60. Propose operating hours of 6 a.m. to 1 a.m. and live entertainment ending by midnight on weeknights and 1 a.m. on weekends. Commit to the Entertainment Commission's Good Neighbor Policy, including community outreach and a noise-complaint protocol. Request that the CUA hearing be scheduled after the Type 42 license escrow is confirmed but before the ABC transfer is finalized, so the Commission can condition approval on the transfer's completion.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 240 to 570 days. Estimated government cost: $8,300 to $24,000. Notes: The critical path is the Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days per the catalog) and the ABC Type 42 license transfer (60–150 days), which must be done sequentially or in parallel depending on Planning's confirmation that the CUA can be filed before the license is escrowed. The Place of Entertainment permit (45–120 days) will run in parallel with the CUA or immediately after. Building permit plan review (14–120 days) and DPH plan check (21–60 days) typically overlap with the CUA hearing process. ABC's timeline may extend by 1–3 months (30–90 additional days) if a Public Convenience or Necessity finding is required due to the nine on-sale licenses within 500 ft. The minimum timeline assumes no PCN delay, over-the-counter DPH and building approvals, and a straightforward CUA hearing with no continuances (about 8 months total). The maximum timeline assumes a PCN referral, full plan review with revisions, a continued CUA hearing, and ABC transfer delays (about 19 months). Government fees include: CUA application (~$3,100–$15,000 depending on construction cost, likely ~$3,100 for interior-only work), POE permit ($2,708), ABC Type 42 license ($1,000–$1,600 state fee, plus the market price of the license itself, which is not a government fee and is not included here), DPH plan check ($828–$2,500), Health Permit to Operate ($470), building permit ($800–$15,000, likely ~$3,000–$5,000 for bar build-out), SF Business Registration ($55–$700, likely ~$95), and state/federal registrations (EIN free, CA entity $70–$150, seller's permit free). Music licensing (ASCAP + BMI ~$600–$5,000/year) and workers' comp insurance are recurring costs, not one-time government fees, and are not included. The cost range reflects uncertainty in building permit fees (tied to construction valuation) and CUA fees (which escalate with project cost). The timeline and cost assume the operator can identify and escrow a transferable Type 42 license from a bar within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD; if no such license is available, no approval path exists and all figures are void.
